items.titleZh: 法拉利让维斯塔潘夺得新加坡站杆位
items.summaryZh: 法拉利车手在新加坡大奖赛排位赛中因微弱差距未能阻止维斯塔潘获得杆位，勒克莱尔和汉密尔顿均有机会阻止维斯塔潘，但最终未能成功。
items.originalTitle: How Ferrari handed Singapore pole to Verstappen
detailZh: 法拉利车手在新加坡大奖赛排位赛中因微弱差距未能阻止维斯塔潘获得杆位，勒克莱尔和汉密尔顿均有机会阻止维斯塔潘，但最终未能成功。
在 Marina Bay Street Circuit 的 Q3 赛段中，维斯塔潘未能改善他的最后一圈成绩，但勒克莱尔的最后时刻冲刺仍不足以逆转局势，而汉密尔顿的速度也比之前慢。
红牛车队终于有一辆赛车，维斯塔潘可以在这条他F1生涯中唯一一条尚未获得杆位或胜利的常规赛道上冲刺到顶端。
不过，不应忽视红牛的明显进步和维斯塔潘自己的出色表现，他对自己的表现描述为'足够获得杆位'是准确的。因为他在这个赛段中并没有最快的赛车，勒克莱尔和汉密尔顿都将哀叹Q3的赛果。
“今天的赛车有夺冠的潜力，但我们没有足够顺畅的练习来完成任务，”勒克莱尔说。 "但马克斯做得更好。"
法拉利车队的两位车手在争夺杆位的过程中都失败了。对于勒克莱尔来说，Q3是在Q1和Q2中挣扎之后的一次巨大救赎，他之所以还能混入其中，唯一的理由是 "我在Q3的最后圈投入了更多"
但可能是那些练习中的刹车问题在他关键时刻困扰了他，因为他承认这 "极大地影响了他的信心"
在13号弯的发夹弯中，他的旋转稍微弱了一些，与汉密尔顿相比失去了近十分之一的时间，以及在16-17号弯的减速弯中过于保守的刹车，这些都是勒克莱尔的败笔。
在16号弯，勒克莱尔在第三部分追回了0.161秒的差距，但在刹车时攻击不够，所以到达时略显不足——正如他在一个理想情况下想要沿着白线滑行通过弯道以最大速度进入并穿过弯道时，前右轮却勾住了内侧的护墙。
但勒克莱尔在中段也并不像汉密尔顿那样强大，因为法拉利的优势在那里无人能敌，所以他并没有在这里追上维斯塔潘，以弥补最后一段的弱势。也许还有进一步的证据表明他在刹车时的不确定性：在几个点上的档位比汉密尔顿高，包括在8号和14号弯时保持在三档，而汉密尔顿则使用了二档。
汉密尔顿看起来在进入弯道时更加从容不迫，Q1和Q2的表现非常出色。他与法拉利非常合拍，真正地发挥了它在刹车和快速进入90度弯道时的出色稳定性。
但尽管他在前两个部分中是最快的，他在Q3中只快了0.033秒。
“Q1和Q2期间，这辆车感觉太棒了，当我完成圈数时，我想，‘她还有更多的潜力’，”他说。
“为了尝试挖掘出这些潜力，唯一的方法就是尝试增加翼片。我认为这让它达到了极限。”
“只是像一个小洞或者类似的东西。之后，这辆车就变得非常敏捷，Q3中的任何一圈都不好。”
“尽管如此，它们加起来还是不错的。汉密尔顿理论上最好的Q3圈速，结合他最好的几个部分，足以获得杆位。”
但是他在第一圈的开局弯角过于松散，在第二圈的最后一个弯角又过于挣扎。
在第一圈，汉密尔顿在第一部分落后于维斯塔潘0.271秒。这是由于他在第一个弯角稍微偏离了极限，然后——这个问题的遗产——在进入第三个弯角之前不得不在第二个弯角收集一小部分时间，随后他猛地锁定了方向盘，导致更大的滑动。
他的中间部分非常出色，比维斯塔潘快了0.273秒。在这个时候，汉密尔顿有望获得杆位，但是他在16号弯稍微过热，这延迟了他切换回动力，以便在第二个弯角的部分重新加速。
在第二次跑道上，一个更整洁的第一部分和一个不错但并不出色的中间部分让他再次进入了最后一部分的比赛，但是他在16号和17号弯的不整洁行驶，以及他在方向盘上的挣扎，使得这一圈比第一圈还要慢。
对于两位车手来说，在另一天或者面对不同的对手，他们的小小失误可能不会让他们失去杆位。但维斯塔潘的实力如此之强，他就像他经常做的那样，很乐意利用其他人的不足。
红牛车队的表现也很好，尤其是在需要更多速度进入的弯道。他的圈速从起点就非常有目的性，前轮在弯道序列的开头非常尖锐，后轮也跟得很紧。但很明显，在中段区域，制动较弱，而且在很多90度慢弯道中，维斯塔潘显然在第七弯道采取了更为谨慎的制动，而在中段区域的其余部分也并不那么令人信服。
在圈速的末尾，这种情况又回到了他身上——在16号和17号弯道，他坚持第三档位，而法拉利的第二档位，这可能暗示了赛车和车手在那里都更加紧密地结合在一起——然后在最后的快速弯道中也表现得稍微更强。
维斯塔潘说：“在整个排位赛中，我们之间的差距非常接近。
“所以，当然，很高兴能站在杆位，因为这正是我想要的。”
“这辆车整个周末都很强劲。当然，总有一些你可以改进的地方，但这对杆位来说已经足够了，所以对此非常满意。”
detailEn: Ferrari's Formula 1 drivers were rightly disappointed to be on the wrong side of a narrow spread in Singapore Grand Prix qualifying as both Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton could have denied Max Verstappen pole.

Just over a tenth of a second separated the trio around the Marina Bay circuit in a Q3 session that had the door left open given Verstappen failed to improve on his final lap - but Leclerc's late leap was not enough, and Hamilton went slower than he had before.
Red Bull finally has a car that Verstappen can hustle to the top spot at the only regular circuit from his F1 career he had not scored a pole or won at prior to this weekend.

But, not to detract from Red Bull's obvious progress, and Verstappen's own quality lap, his description of it being "enough for pole" was exactly right. For he did not have the quickest car in this session and Leclerc, and especially Hamilton, will be lamenting how Q3 played out.
"The car had potential for pole today, but we didn't have a smooth enough session in order to do the job," said Leclerc. "And Max just did a better job."

The Ferrari pair's pole bids failed at different points. For Leclerc, Q3 was a huge salvage job after struggling throughout Q1 and Q2, and the only reason he was in the mix at all was "I just committed a little bit more in Q3 on the last lap".
But it was probably the spectre of braking issues in those sessions that haunted him when it counted, as he conceded it was "taking off quite a lot of confidence".

Bleeding time in the Turn 13 hairpin, where he lost almost a tenth compared to Hamilton with slightly weak rotation, and being too conservative braking for the Turn 16-17 chicane were Leclerc's undoing.

For Turn 16, where Leclerc lost the bulk of his 0.161s deficit to Verstappen in sector three, he just did not attack enough under braking so arrived slightly undercooked - as evidenced by hooking his front right wheel over the inside kerb at a corner you ideally wanted to be just gliding past it along the white line to maximum speed into and through the corner.

But Leclerc was also generally not quite as mighty as Hamilton through the middle sector, where the Ferrari's superiority was unchallenged, so he did not quite gain enough on Verstappen here to offset the weaker final sector. There was perhaps further evidence of his uncertainty under braking: holding a higher gear than Hamilton at a few points around the lap, including leaving it in third for Turns 8 and 14, which Hamilton took in second.

Hamilton has looked a lot more comfortable being so aggressive on corner entry, and was electric through Q1 and Q2. He was much more at one with Ferrari and really extracting the most of its impressive poise under braking and sharp front end into the slower, 90-degree corners especially.
But having been quickest in the first two segments he only managed to go 0.033s quicker in Q3.
"The car felt amazing in Q1 and Q2, and when I finished the laps, I was like, ‘she's got more in her'," he said.
"And the only way in order to try and extract that is to try and add wing. I think it just tipped it over the edge.
"It was only like one hole or something like that. After that the car was just snappy, and none of the laps in Q3 are any good."
Combined they were, though. Hamilton's theoretical best Q3 lap, combining his best sectors, would have been good enough for pole position.
But he was too loose through the opening corners of the first lap and too scrappy in the final sector of the second.

On his first lap, Hamilton shipped 0.271s to Verstappen in sector one. This was by virtue of being slightly wide of the apex into the first corner and then - a legacy of this - having to gather up a small moment through Turn 2 before a much bigger slide followed as he cranked the lock on chucking it into Turn 3.

His middle sector was magnificent, 0.273s quicker than Verstappen. At this point, Hamilton was on for pole - but being ever so slightly hot into Turn 16 just delayed him getting back on the power as he switched back for the second part of the chicane.

On the second run, a tidier first sector and a good but not great middle sector had him in the mix again going into the final part of the lap but an untidy run through 16 and 17 again, with Hamilton sawing at the wheel, meant the lap ended up even slower than the first.

For both drivers, on another day or against a different rival, their small imperfections may not have cost pole. But Verstappen was so strong that he - as he often does - gladly took advantage of others not doing as good a job.

And the Red Bull looked good, too, especially through corners that required a bit more speed on entry. His lap started very purposefully with the front end nice and sharp through the opening sequence of corners and the rear keeping up well. But it was clearly weaker braking and getting the front in for a lot of the 90-degree slower corners in the middle sector, with Verstappen evidently more cautious braking for Turn 7 and then never quite as convincing through the rest of the middle sector.

It came back to him at the end of the lap - and holding third gear to the Ferraris' second into Turn 16 and 17 was perhaps a hint at how both car and driver were just more hooked up there - before ending the lap slightly stronger through the fast final corner too.
"The margins are very close between us throughout the whole of qualifying," said Verstappen.
"So, of course, very happy to be on pole because this is the one that I wanted.
"The car has been pretty strong all weekend. Of course, there are always things that you look into that can be better, but it was enough for pole, so very happy with that."

items.originalTitle: George Russell owns up to Singapore F1 crash: ‘A very bad day because of my own mistake’
detailZh: 乔治·拉塞尔承认新加坡大奖赛事故：‘因我自己的错误，非常糟糕的一天’
拉塞尔在冲刺赛中发生撞车退赛，并且这可能会影响他在排位赛中的表现
梅赛德斯一级方程式车手乔治·拉塞尔承认，是他自己的错误导致他在新加坡大奖赛冲刺赛中发生撞车退赛——这一事故可能影响了他排位赛的表现
作为发车第一排的起跑者，拉塞尔在湿滑的滨海湾赛道上以比杆位车手马克斯·维斯塔潘更好的起步冲到了领先位置，但在最后弯道出口略微跑偏后失去了控制。这位英国车手在撞上内墙后退出了比赛。
正如他在发车线的第二位所展示的那样，拉塞尔在冲刺排位赛中表现迅速，但在主排位赛中他最好的成绩只能排在第六位，他认为这归因于他的机械师不得不匆忙地重建他的银箭赛车。
“显然，这是一整天都非常糟糕，而且起因于我自己的错误，”拉塞尔评论道。
“赛车感觉不太一样。我在后部挣扎，然后我又过热了轮胎，这就像是一个下滑的螺旋，而昨天一切都很顺利，所以我们需要看看为什么会有这样的变化。
“有时候，当整个团队都在快速重建赛车，并且显然已经撞到墙时，这并不令人惊讶。昨天我们每圈都很有竞争力，而今天并非如此。”
这是一个梅赛德斯车队负责人Toto Wolff可以支持的理论，尽管车队仍然需要深入研究。
“与乔治一起，赛车直到最后一分钟才完成，”Wolff对天空体育德国频道说，“地板可能并不完全符合要求。所以总的来说，这是一次不错的表现。”
当被问及他在比赛中能有什么目标时，拉塞尔犹豫不决，由于他在雪邦的引擎故障导致的动力单元处罚，他被降级到最后一排发车位置。
28岁的车手意识到，虽然基米·安东内利在意大利大奖赛中从第19位发车一路冲到胜利，但在阿塞拜疆，他用了17圈的时间从第16位发车位爬升到前十；诚然，这位年轻人‘在巴库的街道上开车像他的祖母一样’。
所以，拉塞尔认为新加坡大奖赛的主要比赛有什么是现实的，Motorsport.com问道？到目前为止，梅赛德斯在本周末被红牛和法拉利挑战得非常艰难，这位英格兰人只是希望获得积分。“这将是非常具有挑战性的，”他补充道。
“基米显然有一场比赛从第19位起步并获胜，另一场比赛从第16位起步，但在最后10圈或 whatever 时只排名第10。同一个车手，同一辆车，但结果却非常不同。所以回答你的问题，我真的不知道。
detailEn: George Russell owns up to Singapore F1 crash: ‘A very bad day because of my own mistake’
Russell crashed out of the sprint as he was leading the race, and it may have impacted his qualifying performance

Mercedes Formula 1 driver George Russell conceded it was his own mistake that led to him crashing out of the Singapore Grand Prix sprint race – an accident which may have hindered his performance in qualifying.

Front-row starter Russell surged into the lead on a wet Marina Bay track with a much better getaway than polesitter Max Verstappen, but lost control as he ran ever so slightly wide on the exit of the last corner. The Briton spun into the inside wall and retired from the race.

As shown by his second place on the grid, Russell had been quick in sprint qualifying, but he couldn’t do better than sixth in the main qualifying session, which he believes is down to his mechanics having to hastily rebuild his Silver Arrow.
“Obviously a very bad day all in all, and stemming from my own mistake,” Russell commented.

“The car didn't feel quite the same. I was struggling with the rear end and then I was overheating the tyres and it was just a bit of a downward spiral, whereas yesterday it all just clicked and it was all working well, so we need to see why that was.

“[This] is not, sometimes, a surprise when the whole team is putting it back together so quickly and it's obviously been in the wall. Yesterday we were competitive every lap we did, and today it was not the case.”
That’s a theory that Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff can get behind, even though the squad still needs to look into it.
“With George, the car was only finished at the very last minute,” Wolff told Sky Germany. “The floor is probably not quite as it should be. So all in all, it was a good performance.”
Asked what he could aim for in the race, Russell was indecisive, with a power unit penalty – ensuing from his Sepang engine failure – relegating him to the back of the grid.

The 28-year-old is aware that while Kimi Antonelli stormed to victory from 19th in the Italian Grand Prix, in Azerbaijan it took him 17 laps to climb from 16th on the grid back into the top 10; admittedly the youngster was ‘driving like his grandmother’ in the streets of Baku.

So what does Russell think is realistic for the main race in Singapore, Motorsport.com asked? With Mercedes more than challenged by Red Bull and Ferrari so far this weekend, the Englishman is merely hoping for points. “It's going to be very challenging,” he added.

“Kimi obviously had one race starting in 19th and won, and another race in 16th and was only up to P10 with 10 laps remaining or whatever. Same driver, same car, but very different outcomes. So to answer your question, I really don't know.”

事故可能影响了他排位赛的表现
keyPointsEn: The crash may have been caused by running slightly wide on the exit of the last corner

items.originalTitle: Isack Hadjar demands massive red Bull engine changes: “Everything is breaking apart”
detailZh: 伊萨克·哈德贾要求红牛进行大规模引擎更换：一切都在崩溃
伊萨克·哈德贾在新加坡连续遭遇两次机械故障后要求更换全新引擎池
劳伦特·梅基斯，红牛赛车队Principal，伊萨克·哈德贾，红牛赛车
对于红牛车迷来说，关注红牛赛车，了解F1新闻，车手更新，技术洞察和米尔顿凯恩斯的赛事分析
红牛车队在2026年新加坡大奖赛中遭遇了巨大的命运起伏。虽然马克斯·维斯塔潘成功为周日的正赛赢得了杆位，但他的队友伊萨克·哈德贾在滨海湾街道赛道的照明下经历了绝对的机械噩梦。
在周六早些时候的冲刺赛中，哈德贾遭遇了致命的动力单元故障，被迫退赛。红牛车队的机械师们在傍晚的排位赛之前完成了惊人的、匆忙的努力来更换发动机部件。然而，这些快速修复并没有持续。
在Q1阶段，哈德贾通过车队无线电报告说，他的发动机熄火了，迫使他一瘸一拐地返回维修区。在随后的尝试中，由于二级变速箱故障，他完全失去了所有的档位。因此，这位法国车手未能设置出代表成绩的时间，正式以第22名的成绩垫底——尽管由于之前对梅赛德斯车手乔治·拉塞尔施加的强制引擎处罚，他实际上将从第21位发车。
当天空体育F1主持人克雷格·斯莱特问哈德贾，知道变速箱故障不是他的错是否让灾难性的结果更容易接受时，哈德贾完全否定了这个观点。
“不，我想开车。说实话，我不在乎P22。我只是想出去做我的事情。开始吧，”哈吉尔说道。
这位愤怒的车手特别沮丧，因为他觉得赛车有足够的速度通过淘汰赛，却浪费了宝贵的赛道时间。
“我现在车库里有很多软胎，它们将不会被使用，”哈吉尔强硬地指出。“这正是我最生气的地方。我只想在那里和其他人战斗。”
鉴于他已经从赛道最后面开始发车，为了全新的机械部件而故意降级发车位置，对于位于米尔顿凯恩斯的车队来说，这似乎是一种非常合理的策略。当斯莱特建议增加一个全新的动力单元到他的年度分配中时，哈吉尔完全支持这个激进的举动。
“是的，当然。我们需要一些新的东西，”哈达尔确认说。'显然，明天是一个机会，因为本周末一切都在崩溃。是的，我们需要一个全新的开始。'
红牛车队负责人劳伦特·梅基斯尚未正式确认车队是否会违反停机规定来安装一个全新的动力单元，但车队巨大的可靠性问题无疑将是其夜间简报的重点。
detailEn: Isack Hadjar demands massive red Bull engine changes: “Everything is breaking apart”
Isack Hadjar demands a completely fresh engine pool after suffering back-to-back mechanical failures in Singapore
Laurent Mekies, Red Bull Racing Team Principal, Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing
For Red Bull fans. Keeping watch on Red Bull Racing, with F1 news, driver updates, technical insight and race analysis from Milton Keynes.

Red Bull Racing is experiencing massively contrasting fortunes at the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix. While Max Verstappen successfully secured pole position for Sunday's main event, his team-mate, Isack Hadjar, endured an absolute mechanical nightmare under the floodlights of the Marina Bay Street Circuit.

After suffering a terminal power unit failure that forced him to retire from Saturday's earlier Sprint race, the Red Bull mechanics completed an incredible, hurried effort to replace the engine components ahead of the evening qualifying session. However, the rapid repairs simply didn't hold up.

During Q1, Hadjar reported over the team radio that his engine had shut off, forcing him to limp back to the garage. On a subsequent attempt to set a lap, he completely lost all of his gears due to a secondary gearbox failure. As a result, the French driver failed to set a representative time and officially qualified dead last in 22nd place - though he will actually start 21st due to a mandatory engine penalty previously applied to Mercedes driver George Russell.
When asked by Sky Sports F1 presenter Craig Slater if knowing the gearbox failure wasn't his fault made the disastrous result easier to digest, Hadjar completely dismissed the notion.
"No, I want to drive. Honestly, I don't care about P22. I just want to get out there and do my thing. Get to it," Hadjar stated.
The furious driver is particularly agitated about wasting premium track time when he feels the car possesses the underlying pace to advance through the elimination rounds.

"I have plenty of soft tyres in the garage right now that are not going to be used," Hadjar aggressively noted. "And that's what pisses me off the most right now. I just want to be there and fight with the other guys."

Given that he is already starting at the very back of the grid, taking additional, intentional grid drops for brand-new mechanical components seems like a highly logical strategy for the Milton Keynes-based squad. When Slater suggested adding a fresh power unit to his yearly allocation pool, Hadjar fully endorsed the drastic move.
"Yeah, for sure. We need stuff that is new," Hadjar confirmed. "And tomorrow is an opportunity, obviously, because everything is breaking apart this weekend. Yeah, we need a fresh restart."

Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies has yet to formally confirm if the team will break parc fermé regulations to install a completely new power unit, but the team's massive reliability issues will undoubtedly be the central focus of its overnight debrief.
